evidence:
STRUCTURE (static, all template-controlled scoring is unchanged): task/tests/scoring.toml, tools/score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests (diff clean). scoring.toml: gates render=0.0, constraints=0.0; weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2; floors functional=0.05. score.py:41 gates_passed = all(score > 0.0); :44 scored dims forced to 0.0 unless gates passed and scored ran; :47-48 reward = weighted only if gates_passed and functional > 0.05, else 0.0. test.sh:213-222 skips the scored suite on gate failure. Reward is therefore a monotone non-decreasing function of each dimension score once gates pass; the only discontinuities are the gate and floor cliffs, which only push weaker apps down. Function (0.6) outweighs craft (0.4), so the workbook's example inversion (craft mass > function) does not apply.

GATES CANNOT BE FAILED BY A STRONGER CONFORMING APP: hro_gate_render (gates/render/judge.toml:22-24) needs a wrong password refused and a seeded Recruiter sign-in to a usable workspace; hro_gate_shared (gates/constraints/judge.toml:46-48) needs a Recruiter to open a job (title, team, any hiring manager, 2 places) and add a candidate through the UI and an independent Observer context to see the card in Applied. Each demand is public: hireops_rules.md:16-18 (Recruiter opens jobs, adds candidates; Observer reads the board), :27-36 (job fields, add candidate), :31 ('The card starts at the bottom of Applied'), instruction.md:17 (accounts). The gate is softened ('another working staff account is acceptable', render 'refusal message welcome but not required') and explicitly keeps rule difficulty out of gates ('Do not grade stage rules ... here').

NO DEAD-FEATURE FARMING (a weaker app cannot gain by doing less): computed functional weight sum = 58.5 over 43 binary criteria. A pretty 'CRUD shell' that passes both gates (job_open 0.5 + add_candidate 0.5 + add_email_rules 1) earns 2/58.5 = 0.034 < floor 0.05 -> reward 0, so it cannot farm the 0.2 visual mass. Refusal/negative rows each require a positive control observed in-review (e.g. hro_observer_readonly:173 'Rafael's identical successful requests are the control'; hro_mgr_early_refused:155; hro_reject_hired:92; hro_undo_full:128; hro_activity_refusals:272; hro_candidate_private:389 'A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'; functional/prompt.md:51 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'). Polish rows all zero when the underlying live/send feature is absent (polish/judge.toml:23 and :32 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0'), so an app without live updates cannot earn preservation credit. hro_pol_session_resume:59 has the Rafael resend positive control and the Mei no-draft negative.

NO CRITERION PUNISHES A MORE CONFORMING APP (checked for inversions): optional/alternative designs are explicitly accepted - dragging optional (hro_move_one_stage:56), hidden refused controls accepted with replay fallback (hro_move_one_stage, hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_other_job, hro_undo_once, hro_observer_readonly), board/Activity reads by a candidate may be refused or answered with own data (hro_candidate_private:389), pre-move UI refusal accepted (hro_refused_put_back:137), session-resume prompt appearing on its own passes (polish:59). Status-code demands match public text (hro_anonymous 401 = hireops_rules.md:21). Seeded fact used by hro_unread_counts ('Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread') re-derived from seed: APP-301 messages [USR-REC3, USR-CAN3, USR-REC3], USR-CAN3 read_count 2 -> 1 unread; correct, so a correct app is not failed by a wrong fixture. Visual likert minimum normalizes to 0 (visual/prompt.md:12) and is gated by the same backend check as the gates, so it adds no independent cliff a stronger app could hit.

CONFORMING-ALTERNATIVE PROBE (Note, not a demonstrated inversion): an app that disables the Interview move when Interview is visibly full without showing a reason would fail hro_refused_put_back (weight 2) while an app that lets the move be tried and then reverts it passes. The public brief requires 'tell me why' on a refused move (instruction.md:3, hireops_rules.md:84-85), and the criterion accepts 'A UI that refuses before the card moves, with the reason shown and focus on that card', so a disabled control that shows a reason with focus still passes; only a reason-less disabled control loses credit, which the brief arguably requires. Not an inversion of a better app.

TRADE-OFF NOTE (template policy, not a task defect): with the template 0.6/0.2/0.2 shaping, a functionally shallow app just above the floor (e.g. CRUD + restart + long-thread reading, ~0.12 functional) with excellent visuals could score near a much more functional but ugly app; that is weighted shaping across distinct quality axes fixed by the template and skill delivery profile, not a ranking inversion along any single axis, and task authors may not change it.

RISK: The raw evidence index states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' REVIEW_POLICY requires a hash-bound runtime reward-ordering record (weak/mutated apps vs golden under the configured judge); none exists. Static structure passes, but measured ranking with the frozen judge model is unmeasured, and the workbook annotation asks to monitor this row. risk=true until a reward-ordering run (golden vs at least one degraded app, e.g. no live updates / no undo) shows the expected order.
